title: Needlepoint TPS Thermometer and Regression Canary for Core LLMs
creator: Marco Nguyen
description:
Goal: Build and maintain a compact, low-noise TPS microbenchmark (the 'Needlepoint Thermometer') that detects sub-5% tokens/sec regressions and p95 latency shifts for our core serving models. Scope: steady-state sustained runs, controlled microbursts, concurrency sweeps, and KV-cache-warm vs cold scenarios. Outputs: per-run aggregated metrics (tokens/sec, median/95/99 latency, failure rates), time-series for trend detection, and a regression detector that can automatically open a Linear ticket or trigger a canary rollback.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reproducible harness that runs in CI and on Dedicated infra with <3% measurement noise for 30s steady-state runs.
- Automated p95 and TPS drift detection with configurable thresholds and signal smoothing.
- KV cache warmup protocol that mimics production prefix reuse and can run in <5m warmup for each model.
- CI check that fails when a model's TPS delta >5% or p95 delta >10% relative to baseline for the same commit.
- Grafana dashboard and an alerting rule that triggers PagerDuty when a sustained anomaly is detected across 3 runs.

Design notes & trade-offs: We will use a mixed synthetic corpus combining short (<=64 tokens) and long (512+ tokens) prompts to surface both attention kernel and memory effects. To reduce noise from autoscaling and noisy neighbors, test VMs will be pinned and network jitter will be sampled from the infra telemetry to exclude outliers. We opted for statistical-smoothing (EWMA) with an adjustable alpha to avoid spurious alerting in microbursts; this trades some sensitivity for fewer false positives.

Instrumentation: metrics emitted to Prometheus via pushgateway during CI runs; StatsD for microbench local runs. Key metrics: tokens_emitted_total, tokens_per_second_sample, request_latency_ms_bucket, kv_cache_hit_ratio, inference_errors_total. Regression detection uses a simple rolling baseline and Bayesian online changepoint detection prototype (proof-of-concept in PR gh-4871).

Deliverables & rollout plan: 1) Minimal harness + baseline profiles for 3 core models (small, medium, large) -> internal alpha; 2) Integration with CI gates and nightly regression scan; 3) Auto-ticketing + canary rollback hook for Dedicated.

Risks: Synthetic prompts may miss rare production patterns; autoscaler interference can mask regressions; tight thresholds will require periodic recalibration.

Next steps (short): finalize corpus (owner: Aisha), land KV-warmup script (PR gh-4871), add Prometheus exporters (PR gh-4923), and prototype alerting rule in staging Grafana (dash link below).
